Subject: Multi-cloud SKU phasing & co-sell enablement — proposed staggered rollout

Team —

Following our sync with Acme yesterday, I sketched a lightweight phased approach for listing SKUs across GCP/AWS/Azure and the corresponding co-sell readiness steps. The goal is to limit scope on wave 1 so we can validate listing mechanics and partner workflows before expanding SKU coverage. Attached: Acme_SKU_matrix.xlsx (matrix + proposed SKU mapping).

Proposal (high level):
1) Wave 1 (canary, 6 weeks): GCP listing only — offer two SKUs: "starter" (hosted, pay-as-you-go) and "pro" (reserved/dedicated small) in us-east and us-west. Reason: fastest sandboxing and simpler co-sell path for the Acme proof-of-concept.
2) Wave 2 (+4 weeks): AWS marketplace listing — bring "pro" + "dedicated-1" packaging. AWS requires partner marketplace manifest + security attestation (Marissa, see checklist). Target regions: us-east-1, eu-west-1.
3) Wave 3 (+8 weeks): Azure — full SKU set including "dedicated-2" (compliant packages with BYOK). Azure listing will require additional VM SKU mapping and marketplace pricing tier mapping.

Key decision points:
- Which exact SKU variants do we want live for wave 1? (I propose Starter & Pro only)
- Region prioritization for each cloud (I suggested us-east/us-west for canary; we should confirm with Acme team)
- Packaging differences: do we want a single binary artifact per SKU or cloud-specific packaging? (cost & ops trade-off)
- Co-sell enablement checklist ownership (Marissa ops / Ben pricing / Soojin legal)

Timeline: 6 week canary -> iterate -> +4 weeks AWS -> +8 weeks Azure.

Immediate asks: please review the attached SKU matrix and reply with: 1) any blockers 2) suggested changes to the wave 1 SKUs 3) confirmation on who will own the marketplace manifest for each cloud.

Thanks —
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Rishi —

Thanks for the clear plan. Quick thoughts:
- Acme is heavily AWS-first (their infra is 80% aws). I'd argue for an AWS canary in parallel with a narrow GCP listing rather than delaying AWS until wave 2. That helps co-sell motion with Acme faster.
- For wave 1 SKUs, keep them minimal: "starter" (SaaS, no BYOK), "pro-basic" (metered + support). Hold dedicated SKUs for post-canary to reduce ops overhead.
- Packaging: prefer a single artifact where possible; cloud-specific manifest layers are fine but let's avoid duplicating runbooks.
- I'll own legal gating and packaging notes for Azure (I can prep a short checklist of VM sizes + BYOK constraints).

I'll update the SKU matrix with an AWS-first alternative and push to the Drive link by EOD.

— Soojin
